correctness.rationale: For any finite field, every nonscalar 2-by-2 matrix is cyclic and its centralizer consists uniquely of uI+vA. Hence all commuting nonscalar family members are affine functions with v!=0. Fixed trace/determinant characterize the nonscalar similarity orbit. A conjugate C=[[a,b],[c,t-a]] meets all entries of all components iff a avoids the forbidden diagonal set E and the roots Z of X²-tX+d and bc=a(t-a)-d is nonzero; exactly q-1 nonzero pairs (b,c) exist for each allowed a. Thus the exact orbit count and basis multiplicity follow. The bound |E|<=2k and |Z|<=2 proves q>2k+2 suffices. Translation pair partitions in F_{2^m} give sharp equality counterexamples for m>=3; an explicit F5 pair has E∪Z=F5 but each individual count eight. Python verification independently enumerates all trace/determinant strata over q=2,3,4,5,7,8,9,11; all scalar-shift pairs for q<=5, triples q<=4, explicit F5 and F8 obstructions; VERIFY_OK. The unrestricted proof does not rely on the finite tests.

originality.rationale: The 2026 motivating preprint addresses fully-nonzero conjugation for a single finite-field matrix; its simultaneous-conjugacy theorem is quaternionic, so it does not imply the finite-field count or characteristic-two obstructions. Sharma (2016) counts commuting simultaneous similarity classes without entrywise nonvanishing. Bodine–McDonald (2012) studies existence of one fully-nonzero characteristic-polynomial realization. Thus no inspected statement implies the exact tuple-dependent forbidden-set formula or its sharp joint obstructions. Targeted public and mathematical-record searches did not return a matching stronger statement, but absence from search is not proof and unread older full text remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: The full text of Bodine–McDonald was not accessible from consulted public sources and might contain an equivalent simultaneous statement not present in its abstract.
An equivalent simultaneous prescribed-pattern theorem might be buried in older zero-nonzero matrix pattern literature; targeted searches cannot exclude all historical statements.
No independent audit has been performed.

value.rationale: The exact count solves the natural joint coordinate-support problem for all commuting nonscalar matrix tuples in the first nontrivial dimension. It provides an explicit existence decision, number of admissible bases, success probability and a universal q-versus-k threshold with infinitely many equality obstructions. The F5 pair shows genuine failure of the inference from individual to simultaneous full support even in a field where every nonscalar two-by-two matrix has a full-support conjugate. These are structural consequences, not an arbitrary table or routine extension of a single-matrix statement.
